title: "Father Divine!" the Saviour Cried
description: "Father Divine!" the Saviour Cried in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 130, “"Thy Will, Not Mine, Be Done."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "Fa-ther di-vine!" the Sa-viour cried, While hor-rors pressed on ev-ery side, And pros-trate on the ground he lay, "Re-move this bit-ter cup a-way.

lines: While horrors pressed on every side,
And prostrate on the ground he lay,
"But if these pangs must still be borne,
Or helpless man be left forlorn,
I bow my soul before thy throne,
And say, — Thy will, not mine, be done!"
Thus our submissive souls would bow,
And, taught by Jesus, lie as low;
Our hearts, and not our lips alone,
Would say, — Thy will, not ours, be done!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
